issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double). Moreover, the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int), which does not match the Pneumatic interface in the solution — a compile-time mismatch. The template's Pneumatic.java is empty, but students will follow the UML which expects an int parameter. This inconsistency across problem, template and solution (and internally inside the solution) will confuse students and cause implementation and compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface signature consistent with the UML/problem statement and its implementations. Change Pneumatic.raisePressure to accept an int parameter (void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease)) and update any implementing classes to use the same signature. Alternatively, if the design should use double, update the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes accordingly — but ensure all three artifacts (problem, template, solution) and implementations use the exact same parameter type.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies Pneumatic.raisePressure with an int parameter (raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int)), but the provided solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) while the solution implementations (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int). This mismatch in the method signature across problem statement and solution artifacts creates confusion about the expected API and which signature students should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the raisePressure method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the Pneumatic interface in the solution to use int raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to match the UML/problem statement and the implementations, or (B) update the problem statement (and any implementations) to require double if that type is preferred. Ensure template, problem text, interface, and implementing classes all use the same parameter type.
